newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi wins vote, faces legislative logjam.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi wins vote, faces legislative logjam.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won its second confidence vote within a week on Wednesday and said it was prepared to call many more such motions before the end of the year in the face of parliamentary blocking tactics.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi called the vote in the lower house to sweep aside some 300 amendments which the separatist Northern League party had attached to a decree covering development projects.
Governments have previously been able to sidestep such filibustering by reissuing decree laws when they expired.
But a recent Constitutional Court ruling banned this practice, leaving Prodi with a legislative nightmare as some 20 cabinet draft laws near their expiry date.
Environment Minister Edo Ronchi told reporters the government was ready to call do-or-die confidence motions for all the decrees unless opposition parties cooperated.

The coalition is also believed to be preparing confidence motions on its 1997 austerity budget which is due to go before the lower house on Friday and faces thousands of amendments both from the League and the main centre-right opposition bloc, the Freedom Alliance.

The Alliance, led by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, has denounced the use of confidence votes, saying the government was taking advantage of League obstructionism to ignore valid political objections to its draft laws.
"If the government insists on putting everything to votes of confidence we will counterattack with motions of no-confidence," said Giuseppe Pisanu, a member of Berlusconi's Forza Italia party.
Commentators said deteriorating relations between government and opposition over the issue could cause chaos.
"Parliament risks being paralysed," La Stampa newspaper said in a headline on Wednesday.

Prodi's coalition relies for its majority in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on backing from the hard-left Communist Refoundation. So far Refoundation has backed the government on every key vote.
Wednesday's motion was carried by 312 votes to 267, officials said. If a government loses a confidence motion it has to resign.

The disputed decree covered development projects for rundown industrial areas in the northern city of Milan and the southern port city of Naples. Last week Prodi called a confidence motion on a decree outlining a rescue package for a southern bank.

The League, which last month declared 'independence' for the rich north of Italy, said both decrees authorised illegal state handouts to the poorer south. It has promised to carry on with its filibustering in a bid to snarl parliamentary work.
